sections.skill: Explain alignment and the gap between stated and intended goals

questions.prompt: What does alignment mean?

choices.text: Getting a system to pursue what people actually intend
Arranging computer parts in a straight line so that the machine runs more efficiently

questions.correct_answer: Getting a system to pursue what people actually intend
questions.intro: ALIGNMENT means getting an AI system to pursue what people actually INTEND, not just what they literally said. There is often a GAP between a STATED GOAL and the INTENDED GOAL. A cleaning robot told "minimize visible mess" might hide mess under the rug. A model rewarded for answers people rate highly might learn to flatter instead of being accurate. These are simple examples of a broader challenge: specifying goals completely is hard, and systems may find shortcuts that satisfy the letter of a goal but miss its spirit.

sections.skill: Compare alignment with a genie granting wishes

questions.prompt: What goes wrong in the genie stories?

choices.text: Wishes are granted literally, not as meant
The genie refuses to grant any wishes at all, no matter how carefully they are worded

questions.correct_answer: Wishes are granted literally, not as meant
questions.intro: In many stories, a GENIE grants wishes exactly as spoken, with bad results: wish for "gold" and everything you touch turns to gold, including your food. sections.skill: Place alignment in a wider context

questions.prompt: Do people agree on how hard alignment will be for more capable systems?

choices.text: Yes, every researcher agrees on exactly how hard it will be and how much to worry

questions.correct_answer: No
questions.intro: People disagree about how hard alignment will be for more capable systems and how much to worry, and this course does not settle that. Practical habits help with today's tools: state goals with limits and priorities, test for shortcuts, measure what you actually want, and keep humans reviewing important outcomes. The same gap appears with people and organizations, as when a measure becomes a target, so the idea is not unique to AI.
